# Average monthly everyday spending per household, by category and tenure

Files: `monthly_spending_by_category.pdf`, `monthly_spending_by_category.svg` (this file: `monthly_spending_by_category.md`), written by `ob_figures.py` (task T25).

**The data are synthetic.** They were generated by `ob_generator.py` from ONS averages (Family Spending, uprated), FCA Financial Lives 2024 holding rates and stated synthetic assumptions, so this figure describes the generator, not real customers.

## Source data

Source: the 100 files `Analysis/open_banking/persona*.json` (Open Banking Read/Write v3.1 objects; seed 20261107) and `Analysis/open_banking/ground_truth.csv`, written by `ob_generator.py` at commit `4287a78`; read by `ob_figures.py` (commit `unknown` or later). Plot style: `TeXFormat.py` sha256 `a33ce9f67e0a`. No random numbers are drawn here (seed: not applicable).

## Filters, transformations and units

**Everyday spending** = booked card purchases (proprietary codes `DEB` debit card and `PUR` credit card, which carry `MerchantDetails`) from every account of a person, excluding own-account transfers (any transaction whose `TransactionReference` also appears on another transaction of the same person) and excluding one-off purchases. **One-off purchases** = the annual package holiday (`JET2HOLIDAYS`) and the synthetic lumpy purchases (`CURRYS`, `KWIK FIT`, `DFS`) listed in `ground_truth.csv` (`lumpy_purchases`, matched on booking date and merchant, taking the largest amount; lumpy purchases the generator foregoes, three in all, never appear in the transactions). Pending transactions are excluded. Rent, bills, direct debits, standing orders and card repayments are committed payments and are not counted.

Per person: total everyday spending in each category over the 12 months divided by 12 (GBP per month; a person with no
purchase in a category counts as 0). The figure shows the mean across persons with the standard error of the mean,
SE = s / sqrt(n) with s the sample standard deviation (ddof = 1), as error bars. Tenure comes from `ground_truth.csv`
(`tenure`). Other = electronics (5732), post (9402), Amazon and general retail (5999), motor repair (7538), holidays (4722). A person is one household in the generator (a partner is not modelled separately).
Plotted data: [`Analysis/open_banking_figures/monthly_by_category.csv`](../../Analysis/open_banking_figures/monthly_by_category.csv)
(per-person values: [`monthly_by_category_per_person.csv`](../../Analysis/open_banking_figures/monthly_by_category_per_person.csv)).

## Statistics

Error bars are standard errors of the mean across persons, as defined above. No tests were run (not applicable); the
tenure groups are small (22 to 49 persons) and no claim of a difference between them is made.

## Interpretation

The average household spent GBP 653.81 per month on everyday card purchases, of which Groceries was GBP 181.69.
Differences between tenure groups reflect the ONS tenure-specific spending averages used by the generator and the
spread of habits across persons, not behaviour of real customers.
